newsitem.title: USA: US to stiffen reporting on foreign bank drafts.
newsitem.headline: US to stiffen reporting on foreign bank drafts.

text.p: The Treasury Department proposed on Thursday new rules to require reporting of foreign bank drafts that could be used as part of a money laundering scheme.

Treasury proposed a rule that would require filing a report on drafts issued to or made out by a foreign bank on a dollar account maintained by a foreign bank in the United States. The rule will be published in the Federal Register.
Stanley Morris, director of Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, said foreign bank drafts "are vulnerable to manipulation and abuse by money launderers."
A requirement for reporting such drafts would make it easier for criminal investigators to detect and track any illegal proceeds crossing U.S. borders, Morris said.
